tagline.text: A park on a guitar-shaped 650-hectare lake for kayaks and boat rides

location.label: Location
location.text: San Francisco on Pacijan Island in the Camotes Islands; the lake park is run by the municipal government

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱100–700 (per person, entrance, kayak and snacks; ferry extra)

children.text: Lake Danao is a freshwater lake of about 650 hectares on Pacijan Island in the Camotes Islands, described as the largest lake in Cebu province. You can kayak, pedal boat and take a sakanaw cruise on the guitar-shaped lake and picnic in the lakeside park.

Lake Danao lies in San Francisco on Pacijan Island in the Camotes Islands. Wikipedia gives its area as 650 hectares (about 1,600 acres), while other guides say about 649 or 700 hectares, so the figure varies slightly by source, but most agree that it is the largest lake in Cebu province and the only known natural freshwater lake in the Camotes. Some pieces also call it the largest lake in the Visayas. It is shaped like the number eight or the body of a guitar, and six barangays touch its shore.

No definite inlet or outlet is known, and a subterranean spring is presumed to feed the lake. The water is clear and looks green and blue, reflecting the trees and sky, and it is recorded as having a pH of 8.5 to 9.0 and a salinity of 0.0 to 0.5 ppt. Mud and weeds make it look shallow, but locals say it is deep, and one guide says the depth ranges from 0.5 meters to 30 fathoms, so do not try to touch the bottom. In the south are two small islets, Crocodile Islet and Snake Islet, together about 600 square meters.

The place most travelers enjoy the lake is Lake Danao Park, developed and maintained by the municipal government. The picnic area is said to open as early as 6 a.m. and close at 6 p.m., and most guides give the entrance fee as

per person. The park offers kayaks, pedal boats, horseback riding, a large cruise boat called the sakanaw, a small swimming pool and tilapia fishing with grilling, and a storyboard near the picnic area is said to tell a legend of lovers that gives the lake the name "Lovers' Lake." There is also a privately owned entrance around the lake, Green Lake Park.

This guide is for travelers who reach the Camotes from Cebu City or Manila and tour the islands for a day or two. Fees and hours differ by source and many are old, so reconfirm them locally. The lake is not big enough to fill a whole day, so it fits best as a half-day stop combined with Santiago beach, caves and viewpoints on the same island. Everything on Pacijan is linked by motorcycle or tricycle, so getting around is not hard.

blocks.title: Picnic area at the lake park

children.text: Lake Danao Park, run by the municipal government, has tables and chairs, and small stores nearby sell french fries, burgers, shakes, coconut juice and sizzling meats, so it is good for a picnic. Parking is said to be free, and visitors are said to be most numerous from February to June.
Guides give kayaks as about
for 30 minutes and pedal boats as about

for 30 minutes. There are also crocodile boats, duck row boats and fish-shaped boats, and life jackets are lent out. The water is deep, so children may not be allowed on boats, and you should check local rules.
The large motor boat called the sakanaw circles the lake for about an hour and carries up to 15 people, at about
for the boat. You can step onto a small islet to rest, and there is a package for ordering food to eat on board. Children are said to be allowed too.
A speedboat takes up to 10 people to one of the two small islets in about
10 minutes
. One trip report says the author paid about
per person, and the islet is a grassy patch about the size of a basketball court with shade trees. There is not much to do, but it is good for photos.
One guide lists horseback riding at about
, and the park is said to have a small swimming pool open from 6 a.m. to 6 p.m. and a kiddie pool for ages 3 to 7. Swimming in the lake is allowed, but one guide says you must borrow a life jacket.

You can fish with friends and grill the tilapia you catch on the spot. A small fishing fee is said to apply, but I could not confirm the amount. One account also says there are no big fish in the lake.
Arqui's Viewing Deck in Monte Alegre is said to give a full-length view of the lake. Unlike the view from a boat on the water, you can see the guitar shape with your own eyes, so it is worth a stop.

Migratory birds are said to fly in from the east in the cool season, and the park is presented as suited to nature lovers. By the shore you can also sometimes see local residents swimming in the early morning and late afternoon.

items.title: Half-day route
items.subtitle: The lake park and nearby caves

children.text: Take a motorcycle taxi or jeepney from Consuelo Port to the lake park. One guide says it takes 30 minutes or less.
Pay the entrance fee and look around the lake from the picnic area.
Take a kayak or pedal boat for 30 minutes, then visit a small islet by sakanaw or speedboat.
Rest with snacks and drinks from a small store and look at the lake viewpoint once more.
Go on to a nearby cave or beach, or return to Consuelo Port.
One guide says to finish before 11 a.m. to avoid the hottest time, and not to stay long in one place.

items.title: One day of a 2-day Camotes trip
items.subtitle: Combining the lake and beaches on Pacijan

children.text: Rent a motorcycle from your lodging and head to the lake park. One guide says a scooter costs about ₱300 a day plus fuel.
Enjoy kayaking and a picnic at the lake park.
Stop at a cave near the lake and cool off in its water. One guide says this cave is inside the park, while another lists it separately, so confirm its location and fee locally.
Go to the beach at Santiago Bay for lunch and a swim.
Return to your lodging to rest and watch the sunset.
There are many direct flights a day from Manila Ninoy Aquino International Airport to Mactan–Cebu International Airport (CEB), and the flight takes about
1 hour 30 minutes
. Airlines and timetables change by season, so check when you book.
The Camotes have no regular commercial airport, so you must go in by boat from the Cebu side.
From Cebu City Pier 1, OceanJet fast ferries to Poro Port take about
1 hour 30 minutes
and run once or twice a day, with fares given as roughly

Ferry fares and schedules differ by operator and the sources do not agree. Confirm directly with the operator within 48 hours before departure.
Jomalia RORO ferries run several times a day from Danao Port, north of Cebu City, to Consuelo Port, and sources differ at
2–2.5 hours
and
. To reach Danao Port, take a bus or V-hire from the North Bus Terminal, about
1–1.5 hours
Arrive 60–90 minutes before boarding, and if you are loading a vehicle or motorcycle, go 1–2 hours early with your OR/CR ready. In the June–October habagat season, cancellations are frequent.

items.title: From the port to the lake

children.text: Many guides say it is 30 minutes or less by jeepney or motorcycle taxi (habal-habal) from Consuelo Port to the lake park, and one source says about
15 minutes
. Just tell the driver "Lake Danao."
Getting around the island is mostly by motorcycle, tricycle, multicab and a few jeepneys, and one account says app-based taxis and metered taxis are not available.

Lake picnics and boating are most comfortable in the dry months from December to May, and February to June is said to be when most visitors come. It is hot at midday, so go in the morning or late afternoon.

In the June–October habagat season, high waves can cancel ferries between Cebu and the Camotes. The Philippine Coast Guard and Cebu Port Authority are known to suspend sailings in rough seas and typhoons, so leave room in your schedule.

The Camotes have about 22 tourist resorts, and near the public market in San Francisco on Pacijan there is also backpacker lodging. One source listed dorm beds near the San Francisco market at about ₱299 per person and fan doubles from ₱399, and a hostel in Santiago with air-conditioned doubles from about ₱995. None of these may be recent prices, so check again on a booking site.

Small stores inside the lake park sell simple snacks, drinks and grilled food, and you can eat local meals at the market and town eateries. The islands rely on diesel power and are known for frequent outages and unreliable mobile signal, so bring cash and a power bank.
Entrance and boat fees differ by source, so carry plenty of cash.
Arrive at the ferry 60–90 minutes before departure, and do not trust old timetables; confirm with the operator.
Always wear a life jacket in kayaks and boats, and do not try to touch the bottom of the lake.
The midday sun is strong, so bring a hat and sunscreen and finish lake activities before 11 a.m.
One guide says to go early in the morning or late in the afternoon to avoid other tour groups' vehicles.
If you rent a motorcycle, wear a helmet, and note the guide that says a scooter is about ₱300 a day plus fuel.
ATMs are few on the island, and one source says the Development Bank ATM near the Poro market accepts only Visa cards, so bring cash in advance.
On Pacijan, combining the lake, caves and Santiago beach saves travel time.
The lake is deeper than it looks and its bottom is muddy, which is dangerous. Borrow and wear a life jacket to swim and follow the staff's instructions.
In the June–October habagat season, ferries between Cebu and the Camotes can be cancelled and you can be stranded on the island, so leave room in your return schedule.
Fares and timetables differ by source, and old values may be wrong, so confirm locally.
The Camotes often have power outages and weak mobile signal, so bring cash and an offline map.
When using a motorcycle taxi, agree on the fare before riding and ask for a helmet.
The information in this guide covers what several sources could confirm in 2026, and some figures date from 2016 or earlier.
